detail: Gov. Brown signs the Open and Transparent Water Data Act (Dodd), Ch. 506, Stats. 2016. No appropriation.
Water Code Part 4.9 (§§12400–12420) in force.
Eight agencies: DWR, SWRCB, CDFW, Water Quality Monitoring Council, OPR, CNRA, GovOps, Delta Stewardship Council. Stakeholder process began July 2017.
First Progress Report with draft Strategic Plan and three minimum protocols; OWIA v2.0; UC Berkeley/CCST report with 20 use cases. (Exact day not verified.)
data.cnra.ca.gov goes live; ~1,300 datasets by April.
Four goals, 49 actions. Federation of existing portals instead of an RFP for a new platform.
'Sustainable Governance and Funding for Open Water Data' recommends an external consortium.
May Revision: $450k DWR, $200k SWRCB, $150k CDFW from the Environmental License Plate Fund. Only AB 1755 line item found.
SWRCB Resolution 2018-0032 adopts an open data policy.
First civic data challenge (OPR, West Big Data Hub).
13-member council convened by OPR recommends a Water Data Consortium.
Agency secretaries' letter supports the Consortium and commits to federating data.ca.gov and data.cnra.ca.gov.
Orders a Water Resilience Portfolio.
DWR reports the requirement met; Ocean and Water Data Partners federations (~17,000 records) date from 2019.
Dodd's follow-on bill: stream gaging plan, 'upon appropriation.'
Nonprofit authorized by §12410(b) launches at a DWR public meeting; Tara Moran, CEO.
Action 22 'Modernize water data systems': AB 1755 training, compliance, streamlined reporting, SB 19 gages, rebuild water-rights database.
Federated USGS, NOAA, USFWS, USBR, USFS records harvested by keyword.
11 members including 6 state agencies.
DWR, SWRCB, Consortium and EDF partner on an open-source platform and data standards.
One-time 2021-22 funding, plus $30M in 2022-23. Outside AB 1755. (Verify against budget acts.)
Pillar 4: 430 new and 200 upgraded stream gages, water-rights data modernization.

event: Consortium joins Internet of Water Coalition
detail: Inaugural organizational member; California IoW pilots include the FHAB data-ingestion framework.
Consortium report with six recommendations.
Robyn Grimm succeeds Tara Moran.
$10B bond, ~$3.8B for water resilience.
DWR's AB 1755 story map, the main official status record.
Water Board's new water-rights system replaces eWRIMS; ~40,000 records public.
Ch. 210/2025: 9 MAF supply target by 2040, includes improving data.
Bonds 'rarely fund the coordination, governance' that water data needs.
Consortium 'Data for Lunch': DWR, CDT, CNRA Data Center on workforce and platform gaps.
Introduced to amend §§12405–12415 (hatchery data, Aug 2027 deadline); chaptered as a groundwater-fees bill after Senate amendments. AB 1755 changes appear dropped. Unconfirmed.
